chapter: Singers, records and Jammin' the Blues
title: Dating 'Jammin' the Blues'
summary: Edison and Berger debate the year of the Norman Granz film shot by Gjon Mili.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Talking about another great tenor player, Lester Young, I wanted to ask you about that tremendous film that you made with Lester Young…
Yeah, that was made in 1940, I think it was 1940.
Was it 1944, I think. That’s usually the date given.
I thought it was made before Prez went in the army.
‘Cause he was in the army. He stayed in the army until….let’s see, the war started in ’41 didn’t it? This was done in 1940.
Because Jo Jones made it and Jo Jones went to the army.
It couldn’t have been right after they were discharged?
He didn’t come back to the band, Prez didn’t.
Was it something put together when they were no longer in the band, is that possible? ‘Cause Norman Granz had something to do with it…

He was the one produced it. And the photographer for Life magazine did all the work in there, the lighting. In fact, that short won a first prize. Gjon Mili was the guy that was the cameraman and took all the photographs and had all the lighting so wonderful. I think it was done before ’44 because Prez didn’t come back to the band after he came back out of the army. Neither did Jo Jones.
